Definition: An invalid syllogism: all A are B; no C is A; therefore no C is B. The conclusion reaches further than the premises allow, because C could still be B another way.
Example: Someone argues, 'All dogs are mammals. No cats are dogs, so no cats are mammals.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'All prophets spoke for God. No poet is a prophet, so no poet speaks for God' — though poets can still speak truthfully about God.
HowToRespond: Show the overreach: 'The conclusion goes further than the premises allow — let's see what actually follows.'
